title: Hamiltonicity and connectivity thresholds of the random graph G(n, p)
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two classical threshold results for the binomial random graph G(n, p), modelled as a finite product probability space with one independent Bernoulli(p) coin per pair of vertices: Pósa's theorem (1976) that G(n, p) with p ≥ C log n / n is Hamiltonian with probability tending to 1, also stated with the explicit constant C = 80 (posa_eighty), and both sides of the Erdős–Rényi connectivity threshold (1959): G(n, (log n ± ω(n))/n) with ω(n) → ∞, the edge probability clipped to [0, 1], is connected with probability tending to 1, resp. 0. Hamiltonicity and connectivity are Mathlib's SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian and SimpleGraph.Connected. Mathlib defines the binomial random graph as a measure on graphs (SimpleGraph.binomialRandom); this project uses its own finite product model instead, and these threshold theorems are not in Mathlib.
